title: Serve Trace Lattice — Latency Portrait by Model & Route (stream vs non-stream)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a consolidated dashboard and supporting telemetry pipelines that present a compact, queryable "latency portrait" per model and per API route with explicit streaming vs non-streaming (io_mode) breakdowns. The goal is an operator-first view that pinpoints regressions (p50/p95/p99) and links directly into trace hooks and logs for fast root cause investigation. This ticket covers the dashboard panels, metric naming and aggregation conventions, metrics/logs pipeline adjustments to ensure low-cardinality rollups and trace link enrichment, and alerting thresholds for regression detection.
background: Engineering and SRE teams have partial panels split across multiple boards. Investigations are slowed by inconsistent metric dimensions (some endpoints report route, others only endpoint_id), missing io_mode tags for legacy handlers, and lack of direct trace links from percentile tiles. We want a single surface that shows distribution summaries, time-series percentiles, cohort heatmaps, and clickable trace anchors for tail requests.
approach: 1) Define canonical metric schema: telemetry.latency_ms (labels: model, route, io_mode, env, stage). 2) Add a derived gauge telemetry.latency_percentile with percentile label (50/95/99) for pre-aggregated queries where cost matters. 3) Backfill io_mode tagging in the request collector for legacy paths. 4) Add trace_link context to sample tail logs (sampled by p99 and error). 5) Build dashboard panels: percentile ridgeline, delta waterfall (component decomposition), cohort heatmap by request-shape, and tail table with trace links. 6) Create alert rules: p95 increase >20% over 24h baseline or sustained p99 breach. 7) Rollout in two phases: internal dogfood then org-wide release.
data_model_notes: Canonical metric: telemetry.latency_ms{model="<model_name>",route="<route>",io_mode=stream|blocking,env=prod|staging}. Aggregation: histogram to summarize token-level vs total-response latency; rollups: 1m, 5m. Store percentiles via backend summary or approximate sketch to control cardinality.
dashboard_panels: Percentile Mosaic: p50/p95/p99 time series stacked by io_mode and model
Ridgeline Distribution: daily ridgelines per route to visualize shape changes
Cohort Heatmap: latency percentiles binned by request-shape (input tokens, output tokens, prompt vs completion)
Tail Table: top p99 requests with KV cache hit rate, model-version, route, io_mode, and clickable trace link
Waterfall Decomposition: component-level timings (ingest, tokenize, model_infer, postprocess, network) for sampled traces
Regression Delta Widget: shows percentage delta vs 7d and 30d baselines with recommended rollback flag
metric_queries_examples: PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(telemetry_latency_bucket{model="*", io_mode="stream"}[5m])) by (le, model, route))
Tail sampling rule: sample where telemetry.latency_ms > 1200 and rand() < 0.1 -> attach trace_link
trace_integration: Instrument collector to attach a trace_id header for sampled tail traces. Add 'trace_link' field to log_event schema and surface this in tail table. Ensure sampling policy includes error traces and top-n slow requests per minute per route.
pipeline_changes:
- Modify ingest lambda to preserve io_mode label for legacy routes.
- Add a downsampling job that computes telemetry.latency_percentile per 1m bucket and writes to the metrics-store.
- Ensure logs pipeline enriches logs with trace_link when sampling condition met.
alerts_and_slos: Create alert: obs_latency_regression_p95 if p95 > baseline*1.2 for 1h. Create SLO panel mapped to business routes with burn rate calculator. Tie alerts to runbook: check KV cache hit rate, model variant fallback, recent deploys, and region capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard available in Observability > Latency Portrait scoped to model+route
p50/p95/p99 panels update within 60s of metric ingestion
Trace links present for sampled tail rows and open correct trace viewer
Backfilled io_mode tags on >95% of historical 14-day traffic for top 20 routes
Alert rule firing tested with synthetic injection and documented runbook

risks: Cardinality explosion if model and route are both high-cardinality; mitigation: whitelist top-50 models and use rollups for others
Trace sampling might miss causal events; mitigate by deterministic sampling for errors and p99
Downsampler lag could show stale percentiles; keep 1m buckets and instrument pipeline latency
